tit.title: Technical Intern Training
tit.subtitle: Five years to grow a skill — and a life.
tit.overviewBody: The Technical Intern Training Program transfers Japan's skills and know-how to talent from developing nations, supporting their home countries' economic growth. Trainees spend up to five years learning on-the-job in Japan.

faq.a1: Typically 6–8 months from application to arrival, including pre-departure Japanese training, health checks, and visa.
faq.a2: Costs depend on headcount and role. Quotes are free — get in touch.
faq.q3: What Japanese level do trainees have?
faq.a3: JLPT N5–N4 on arrival, with continuous learning support after placement.
faq.q4: What's required of the host company?
faq.a4: Any law-abiding company that can assign qualified instructors and a life-skills supervisor is welcome, regardless of industry or size.

ssw.title: Ikusei-Shuro System
ssw.subtitle: Japan's reformed 2027 program — built for talent and retention.
ssw.overviewBody: Launching in 2027, Ikusei-Shuro is Japan's new foreign-talent program. Designed to balance training and workforce continuity, it grants three years of development with a clear path to the Specified Skilled Worker (SSW) status.

long.title: Long-term career design
long.desc: Move from Ikusei-Shuro to SSW for 10+ years of employment.

skill.title: Stronger Japanese skills
skill.desc: Stepwise Japanese requirements lift on-the-job communication.

stable.title: Stable retention
stable.desc: Clear paths translate into higher retention and morale.
